en.t: This ancient poem appears in the Shūishū.

units.source_text: “舍身”与“航标”，日语读音相同，都读作miotsukushi。

en.t: In Japanese, “sacrificing oneself” and “channel marker” have the same pronunciation: both are read miotsukushi.

units.source_text: 难波地方海中航标特别有名。

en.t: The channel markers in the sea around Naniwa were especially famous.

units.source_text: 此古歌乃就目前所见“航标”而咏为恋爱“舍身”之意。

en.t: This old poem takes the visible “channel marker” before one’s eyes and uses it to suggest “giving oneself up” for love.

units.source_text: 犹如中国诗“东边日出西边雨，道是无晴却有晴”，亦因“晴”与“情”同音而指东说西也。

en.t: It is like the Chinese poem, “sunrise in the east, rain in the west; they say there is no clear sky, yet there is feeling,” where the homophony of “clear sky” and “love” lets the poet speak of one thing while meaning another.

units.source_text: 以下源氏与明石姬唱和的诗，也都根据此古歌。

en.t: The poems exchanged below by Genji and the Akashi lady are also all based on this ancient poem.
